usage: This is the standard way to say 'happy birthday' in Moroccan Darija, understood and used across all ages and regions. It is appropriate for both formal and casual situations. In urban areas and among younger generations, it is also extremely common to simply use the French phrase 'joyeux anniversaire'.

variants.label: French loanword
variants.note: Extremely common among younger people and in urban areas, often used interchangeably with the Arabic phrase.

variants.label: with a blessing
variants.arabic: عِيد مِيلاد سَعِيد، ب طُول العْمَر
variants.english: Happy birthday, with a long life
variants.note: Used to add a traditional blessing for longevity, making the greeting warmer and more affectionate.

variants.label: wishing 100 years
variants.note: A very common Moroccan well-wish said to the birthday person, hoping they live a long life.

examples.english: Happy birthday, we will celebrate today.

examples.arabic: عِيد مِيلاد سَعِيد ل صاحْبِي العْزِيز.
examples.english: Happy birthday to my dear friend.

examples.arabic: واش قَلْتِي لِيها عِيد مِيلاد سَعِيد؟
examples.english: Did you tell her happy birthday?
